h: Shabbos Renews the Enduring Covenant of the Avos and Tribes

p: In the Minchah prayer we say:
Yaakov and his sons will rest on it,"
in the manner of what it says (Vayikra 26:42):
"I will remember My covenant with Yaakov,
and also My covenant with Yitzchak,
and also My covenant with Avraham
"I will remember for them the covenant of the first ones"
this is the covenant of the Tribes,
and this is what they said
"It is a tradition that a tribe is never wiped out";
that the holiness of each tribe remains.
"Why are they listed in reverse order?
Yaakov the small one is worthy, etc."
"Yaakov is the glory of the Avos,
the sum of them all, etc.,
is the completion of the Avos, etc."
(בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה עו, עו, א)
'For Yaakov He chose for Himself, etc.'"
And so here in the Midrash
only in the merit of Yaakov, etc.;
only in the merit of Yaakov."
So why does it say afterward
that they are listed in reverse order
to say that "if there are no deeds in Yaakov,
the deeds of Yitzchak are worthy"?
there is no proof that its intent is
than the deeds of his fathers;
rather, they are listed in reverse order
because each one is worthy on his own,
and had they been listed in order,
that all three covenants are needed together.
The intent of the Midrash may be:
"if there are no deeds in Yaakov"
for Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
was one whose bed was complete,
with no refuse in it at all;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה אַחַר זֶה
and as the Midrash Rabbah says after this
and Yisrael are not so clean
the deeds of Yitzchak are worthy,
except that afterward it became clear
that he is not of his seed,
And in truth Yitzchak was called Yisrael,
And "if there are no deeds of Yitzchak"
who at least was circumcised at eight days,
meaning that he was born in holiness,
the deeds of Avraham are worthy.
and he wanted to bring the whole world
under the wings of the Shechinah,
and he was "father of a multitude of nations"
פֶּרֶק ד מֵהִלְכוֹת בִּכּוּרִים הֲלָכָה ג
which is not so of Yitzchak:
we do not find that he made converts,
only that it is alluded to
in "the land of his father's sojournings" (Bereishis 37:1)
(בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת וַיֵּשֶׁב, פד, ד)
it helped them only during his lifetime,
(as they said in Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer)
so that whoever is of the seed of Yisrael
זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
zecher tzaddik v'kadosh livrachah l'chayei Olam Haba, related
in the name of the holy Rav of Lublin,
זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
zecher tzaddik v'kadosh livrachah l'chayei Olam Haba,
that he drew one convert close
that the convert he pushed away
than the other one whom he drew close.
is in truth of the seed of Yisrael,
and mislead people into thinking he is a convert;
one who is of the seed of Yisrael
only the Torah commanded and warned
to love and draw close even the convert.
the covenant of all the Avos
and the covenant of the Tribes;
and this is the holiness of Yosef,
(וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה עא, ב)
whoever is circumcised is called a tzaddik
the daughter who is crowned with the Avos
and in the Zohar Chadash, Toldos,
as corresponding to the holiness of Yosef.
regarding Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him
and he likewise taught his sons
nevertheless we do not find of him
of whom is written the keeping of Shabbos, etc."
for of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
the keeping of Shabbos is written explicitly.
And likewise of Yosef it is written (Bereishis 43:16):
"'Prepare' means nothing other than Shabbos, etc.;
"And portions were taken to them from before him";
that is, he gave all the Tribes
from the remains of his Shabbos meal,
which corresponds to the holiness of Yaakov,
corresponds to the holiness of Yaakov
the holiness of all the Avos;
and we say, "Yaakov and his sons":
"his sons" is the covenant of the Tribes,
which is the holiness of Yosef,
who instilled the holiness of Shabbos
And he refines all the Tribes
and they are called by his name,

p: praise to God, Creator of the world.
for all the good He has bestowed on me,
and has granted me to bless the completed work,
and to attach myself to holiness
and to bring to the press
the remaining parts of Pri Tzaddik
and the remaining holy manuscripts that are extant.
And for good be remembered the name
of my son, the keen and praiseworthy
David Yehuda HaKohen, may he live,
May the merit of the holy Torah of
זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
zecher tzaddik v'kadosh livrachah l'chayei Olam Haba,
stand for me and for my children
and my children's children forever. Amen.
Words of the one who brought it to the press
